subject: Discovery recap & next steps inference cost pressure (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbot.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps - inference cost pressure (FinBot)

Alex / Priya - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Pain points we heard:
- Unit inference costs are the primary blocker: finance is seeing a blended per-response cost that spikes unpredictably month-over-month.
- Latency variability on peak traffic is causing occasional timeouts for the credit decisioning flow.
- Multiple microservices call the model provider directly; no centralized KV/prefix cache, so duplicate work increases cost.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Heavy batch scoring on on-prem A100s; low-latency surface area uses a commercial hosted API.
- Gateway fans out to multiple model endpoints; no centralized caching layer today.
- Mix of open models (self-hosted) and a paid API for embeddings/reranking.

Success criteria for a pilot:
- Target ~30-40% reduction in per-inference unit cost vs your hosted baseline, with quality degradation <= ~2-3% on your benchmarks.
- 99th percentile latency for the primary route < 150ms.
- Integration via VPC peering or Private deployment with no regressions to customer-facing behavior.

Openness / constraints:
- You're open to quantization (8-bit / 4-bit) provided we validate on your 1.2k benchmark prompts.
- Willing to adopt prefix/KV caching and request deduplication if it shows clear unit-cost benefits and requires minimal infra changes.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with infra: Ben & Dev to join  discuss batching, caching, and quantization validation plan. Target: week of Mar 1.
2) FinBot to share a 72-hour sample of production traffic + baseline cost/latency numbers  Alex to send.
3) Redwood to deliver a mutual action plan (attached) and an initial cost model based on the traffic sample (attached spreadsheet).

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_FinBot_v1.pdf, inference_cost_model_finbot.xlsx

If this aligns I'll loop Ben & Dev to propose calendar times for the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbot.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbot.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 19:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps - inference cost pressure (FinBot)

Thanks Marissa - great write-up and accurate summary. A few clarifications and asks:
- The 30-40% target aligns with what finance needs. Current blended per-response cost we track is ~$0.42; getting to <$0.30 would be compelling.
- Quantization is acceptable as long as product retains quality on our scoring prompts (we have ~1.2k benchmark examples).
- Security/compliance: we'll need a short questionnaire plus an architecture diagram for Private deployment. I will loop in our security lead if needed.

I will provide the 72-hour traffic dump and baseline cost/latency numbers by EOD Friday. For the technical call please include someone who can speak to batching/queueing and cache invalidation semantics.

Alex Johnson
Head of ML Platforms | FinBot
